summary.headline: PhysicsWallah FY26 revenue rose 35% to INR3,900 crore and pre-Ind AS EBITDA tripled to INR300 crore; FY26 PAT was still negative at INR24 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 was the first full year after the November 2025 IPO. Revenue from operations reached INR3,900 crore (+35% YoY), with online up 39% and offline up 31%. Pre-Ind AS EBITDA rose to INR300 crore from INR93 crore, and PBT turned positive at INR10 crore versus a loss of INR259 crore. PAT was negative INR24 crore, against a loss of INR243 crore, after a one-time Labour Code charge and IPO expenses; management said PAT would otherwise have been positive. Q4 revenue was INR919 crore (+51% YoY) and Q4 pre-Ind AS EBITDA was INR9 crore versus negative INR139 crore a year earlier.

segments.name: Online
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 39% YoY in FY26 with over 4.9 million paid students (+20% YoY). Foundation, pre-foundation, CUET, boards and state boards together almost doubled; state boards revenue rose about 9x and Curious Junior about 4x.

segments.name: Offline (Vidyapeeth, Pathshala, other)
segments.commentary: Revenue approx. INR1,775 crore (+31%) across 353+ centres; Vidyapeeth is about 70% of offline revenue. Offline net margin improved from about -19% in FY25 to just under -10% in FY26; 60% of the 116 Vidyapeeth centres are profitable.

segments.name: K-12 schooling
segments.commentary: Strategy moved to 100% asset-light with no further M&A capital; school integration revenue grew about 3x. Management said school revenue is under 1% of total and the company runs single-digit schools under brownfield tie-ups.

segments.name: FinZ NBFC
segments.commentary: INR120 crore equity infusion into a wholly owned NBFC with RBI licence. Prior partner-led loans were about INR200 crore with under 1% NPA; about 80,000 students served, under 2% of paid students.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at more than 30% (offline a couple of points lower than online).
FY27 EBITDA improvement guided at upwards of 100%.
Full-year PAT profitability committed for FY27.
Net offline business guided to be profitable on a full-year basis in FY27; offline steady-state margin target 13-15%, with some centres above 20%.
Offline marketing spend to fall about 20% over the next three years; online to reach 55% of revenue within three years.
Seat utilisation steady-state assumption of 2.25x for the Vidyapeeth cohort (currently about 2x).
Investor day planned for coming months.
capex_capacity: Offline expansion is paused at the end of the current enrolment season; further expansion to be balanced and disciplined after that.
Student-teacher ratio in offline is about 80s; management aims to keep improving it.
K-12 move to asset-light: no capex; school integration uses existing schools.
Capital allocation: selective inorganic deals in online community-led businesses and vernacular capability; management plans to announce large PAT-positive online acquisitions this year.
Saarthi (UPSC) acquisition continues as an independent brand with tech and distribution synergies in progress.
demand_pricing: Vishwas Diwas sales event: collections up 36% YoY to about INR200 crore in roughly three weeks; enrolments up 21% and ARPU up 12%.
Online ARPU up over 11% (ACPU) driven by Infinity, Infinity Pro, Curious Junior and Power Batch; base batch prices broadly unchanged.
Like-for-like Vidyapeeth ARPU up 6-9%; blended offline ARPU fell due to mix shift to short-term courses. Offline enrolments up 42%, revenue up 32%.
Share of standalone offline (Vidyapeeth/Pathshala) in enrolments fell from 80% to 72%.
NEET 2026 cancelled due to paper leak; management expects NEET to move online from FY27, which it sees as an enrolment tailwind.
Earners skilling category: about 100,000 students enrolled in its first month.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 growth acceleration to 50%+ and how much was organic versus Saarthi?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Vishwas Diwas, AI-led engagement and better paid-to-paid conversion. Growth was mostly organic; Saarthi contributed a small amount.

qa_highlights.question: Offline margin trajectory and medium-term steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Offline net margin improved from -19% to just under -10%; management targets full-year net offline profitability in FY27 and a 13-15% steady-state margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is there like-for-like pricing in offline ARPU?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes: like-for-like Vidyapeeth ARPU rose 6-9%, but blended ARPU is slightly down from short-term course mix.

qa_highlights.question: Is K-12 asset-light, and will schools be run?
qa_highlights.answer: Schools are still run, but via brownfield tie-ups in single-digit numbers, under 1% of revenue; no capex and no further M&A capital in K-12.

qa_highlights.question: Can the FY26 EBITDA step-up repeat in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a quarterly number; it guided to upwards of 100% EBITDA growth annually and said Q1 should not be extrapolated.

qa_highlights.question: Seat utilisation steady state and online margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady state for Vidyapeeth is 2.25x seat utilisation; 70% of offline is JEE/NEET. Management agreed online margins should expand as new categories scale because incremental students carry little extra cost.

risks_watch: FY26 PAT is still negative at INR24 crore; full-year PAT profitability in FY27 is a commitment to track.
Offline must reach net profitability in FY27; the Vidyapeeth cohort is about 70% of offline and newer centres (12 months old) are still maturing.
The NBFC lending (INR120 crore equity) moves the company into balance-sheet credit; watch NPA and disbursement scale.
Q3 to Q4 EBITDA seasonality was questioned; management says revenue recognition is weighted to Q2 and Q3.
Refunds and dropouts are under 2% of the group; no breakdown given.
Management's AI-led revenue claims (Socratic AI Tutor, Aryabhatta 2.0) are not yet quantified.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, profitability and online strategy, with repeated focus on online and AI. Management was less precise on segment margins and quarterly cadence, and some answers on Q3 to Q4 seasonality were defensive.
key_quotes: We would have been PAT positive but for one-time expenses of implementation of Labour Code that came earlier this year and IPO expenses.
So, we are guiding on a full-year profitability.
Because every additional student in our online batches is not top line, it's bottom line.
